title: Lutnick Faces Backlash and Job Peril Over Ties to Nvidia and China Chip Export Lapses
snippet: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is drawing intense scrutiny from White House advisers and lawmakers over his close relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and delays in restricting advanced chip sales to China.
content:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is facing mounting pressure inside the West Wing and on Capitol Hill following revelations that his department stalled restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports to China while cultivating a deep relationship with disgraced former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

With Huang’s sudden resignation from Nvidia after counterintelligence probes linked an associate to Chinese state interests, senior Trump administration officials are now questioning whether Lutnick shielded key Chinese-linked entities from federal blacklists against White House directives.

A High-Stakes Alliance Under Fire

Lutnick early on declared Nvidia and its chief executive a "national treasure," helping elevate Huang into a premier White House ally during Donald Trump’s second term. Over two years, Lutnick championed policies that allowed Nvidia to continue selling its downgraded H20 artificial intelligence chips to Chinese buyers—a deal finalized after Nvidia agreed to funnel 15 percent of its China revenues back to the U.S. government.

However, critics within the administration now allege that Lutnick’s department failed to take aggressive action against suspected conduit firms, effectively undermining national security priorities in favor of tech industry interests.

Ignored Intelligence and the Megaspeed Scandal

At the center of the political storm is Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company suspected by intelligence agencies of illicitly diverting high-end American microchips into mainland China. Despite recommendations from the Treasury, State Department, and Pentagon to place Megaspeed on the U.S. Entity List, Commerce officials repeatedly delayed action.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly voiced frustration on Friday, pointing out that multiple agencies favored blacklisting Megaspeed to enforce mandates against sending top-tier chips to strategic adversaries. Key U.S. intelligence officials also briefed lawmakers late last year regarding potential foreign influence efforts aimed at administration policy through associates connected to Huang.

Mounting Congressional Probes and Threats to Tenure

The political fallout has spread quickly to Capitol Hill. Both Republicans and Democrats have demanded access to internal Commerce Department communications, while House committees are preparing closed-door interviews with top export control personnel.

As President Trump prepares for upcoming summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, several key advisers are privately discussing whether Lutnick should be replaced. Though the White House publicly expressed confidence in the Commerce Secretary, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for immediate accountability over what they describe as a major security lapse in the ongoing technological race with Beijing.
